title: Why Hims & Hers Could 100X Your Money
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Travis Hornsby of Asymmetric Investing argues Hims & Hers could 10x or even 100x over 10-20 years, calling it extremely undervalued at about a $6.4B market cap despite positive news, with the stock down 38% over the past year and 8.2% in the past month. He opens with recent news: testosterone/TRT expansion (membership $50/month, injectable TRT $79, oral TRT $179, generic $159), expansion into Germany as part of a wider international push (Canada, Australia via Eucalyptus, Japan as a 100M-person market), and peptides, where an HHS draft interim policy would open BPC-157 and TB500 to compounders and Hims has prepared for years with its own peptide facility, aiming for 100% US-made peptides. He models peptides at $180M revenue at 100,000 subscribers ($50 membership plus ~$100 product) and $1.8B at one million. His five reasons to love the stock are: a huge addressable market (US pharma $400-800B by various estimates), market leadership (51% of observed telehealth sales and 48.5% of customers versus Ro/Roman at about 23-25%), expanding specialties from ED into dermatology, mental health, hormone health and weight loss, international operating leverage under one brand, and peptides as a new growth leg. Calls: HIMS BUY (reiterated from 10 October), with revenue guided to +50% year-over-year in H2 2026 on about $2.6B of current revenue, potentially reaching $5-6B in a couple of years; Q3 earnings due 9 November are the next catalyst. Captions garble Hims & Hers repeatedly, but the numbers and thesis are consistent.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (prior BUY 10 Oct): calls Hims & Hers extremely undervalued and a potential 100x over 10-20 years, despite the stock down 38% over the past year and 8.2% in the past month. Five reasons: a huge US pharma market ($400-800B), market leadership (51% of observed telehealth sales, 48.5% of customers vs Ro/Roman ~23-25%), expanding specialties (dermatology, mental health, hormone health, weight loss, now testosterone/TRT), international expansion (Germany, Canada, Australia via Eucalyptus, Japan potential), and peptides as a new leg (in-house compounding facility, HHS draft interim policy opening BPC-157/TB500, modelled at $180M at 100k subscribers, $1.8B at 1M).
calls.price_at_call: ~$6.4B market cap; ~$2.6B revenue, H2 2026 guidance +50% YoY
calls.base_case: Revenue grows toward $5-6B in a couple of years on peptides plus organic/GLP-1 momentum, justifying a much higher multiple than near-1x sales.
calls.bull_case: 100x over 10-20 years if it becomes a top-2/3 player in a massive disrupted market.
calls.bear_case: International expansion adds execution risk for management; peptides still need final rules written; Q3 earnings due 9 Nov are the near-term catalyst.
